title: A resonant circuit under competing explanations
question: Which of the supplied circuit models is consistent with calibrated amplitude, phase and energy evidence, and what remains unidentified by those observations?
mode: Simulation only. All observations are synthetic. No physical experiment, NU laboratory credit, equipment requirement or pilot validation is implied.

apparatus.required: The free browser activity, a calculator and a place for derivations. The notebook and evidence export are built into the platform.
apparatus.model: A sinusoidal source with known source resistance drives a series inductor, capacitor and resistive load. A selectable finite probe impedance loads the measurement node. The reference output is the load voltage relative to the stated source phase.
candidateScenarios: Baseline linear components with the disclosed source resistance
A changed capacitor value within a supplied range
A finite probe input resistance that changes the observed transfer function
apparatus.limits: The model is lumped, linear, sinusoidal and at steady state. It does not model saturation, dielectric breakdown, stray distributed elements, electromagnetic interference or real instrument protection. Numerical ideal-circuit values are not physical construction instructions.

syntheticMeasurements.provenance: Show a persistent synthetic-data label, dataset identifier, version, seed, units, source/probe settings and observation-generation model. Freeze the observations used in a submitted record.
syntheticMeasurements.calibration: Supply independent known RMS amplitudes and known phase references with bounded readout error. A detector gain/offset and phase offset must be accounted for before interpreting the circuit sweep. Show that a fitted central calibration is not an exact correction when references have uncertainty.
syntheticMeasurements.initialPlanningBounds: Amplitude readout bound 0.003 V and phase readout bound 0.5 degrees, subject to independent feasibility checks before implementation. They are synthetic closed bounds, not standard deviations or physical instrument specifications.
syntheticMeasurements.sampling: Offer a documented finite frequency grid spanning below, near and above the nominal resonance. Learners select a calibration/model-selection subset before revealing held-out frequencies. The final evidence must contain informative observations on both sides of resonance, not only its peak.
syntheticMeasurements.phase: Use a declared source reference and principal phase interval, compare wrapped differences correctly and distinguish phase uncertainty from amplitude uncertainty. A near-zero output cannot support an arbitrarily precise phase claim.
syntheticMeasurements.expectedPattern: Extra series resistance broadens/damps the response; changed capacitance moves the reactive balance; probe loading changes the observed load and amplitude as well as damping. Actual distinguishability must be established by independent fixtures, not assumed from these qualitative descriptions.

procedure.action: State a falsifiable prediction and at least two candidate models before revealing the sweep.
procedure.evidence: A saved prediction with the chosen output, controlled variables and discriminating observation.

procedure.action: Write the circuit equations and sign/amplitude conventions. Derive the transfer function or equivalent real sine/cosine equations.
procedure.evidence: A labeled connection description, component units, current/voltage references and independently checked limiting cases.

procedure.action: Use the independent reference signals to estimate calibration and its admissible uncertainty.
procedure.evidence: Raw calibration records, correction rule, residual bounds and an explanation of what the calibration cannot identify.

procedure.action: Choose informative model-selection frequencies and reserve held-out frequencies.
procedure.evidence: A recorded selection made before held-out reveal, with a reason for samples below, near and above resonance.

procedure.action: Generate each candidate's amplitude and phase predictions and compare them with corrected observations.
procedure.evidence: An exportable table of raw/corrected values, candidate predictions and residual/uncertainty intervals. Rejected candidates need a specific failed observation.

procedure.action: Audit energy using source power, each resistive loss and reactive exchange. Cross-check at least one state in the time domain.
procedure.evidence: A power ledger with consistent peak/RMS conventions and a separate time-averaged or analytic check; refinement evidence for numerical integration.

procedure.action: Reveal and evaluate held-out data without silently refitting the selection model.
procedure.evidence: A preserved original prediction and held-out comparisons. If revision is needed, identify it as a new version and explain the changed assumption.

procedure.action: Write a supported conclusion, competing explanations and limitations, then self-assess and submit the report.
procedure.evidence: A reproducible saved report with dataset/version, settings, exported observations, calculations and rubric evidence. A new revision preserves the prior submitted record.

rubric.scale: Each criterion is scored 0-3 by the learner. Zero means missing evidence; one means an assertion or incomplete account; two means complete, technically consistent evidence; three additionally explains an independent check, alternative or meaningful limitation.

criteria.title: Prediction and controlled comparison
criteria.adequate: Defines an observable prediction and a sample design that could distinguish at least two models.

criteria.title: Synthetic provenance and calibration
criteria.adequate: Preserves raw references and observations, states synthetic provenance and carries calibration uncertainty into comparisons.

criteria.title: Circuit derivation and conventions
criteria.adequate: Uses a coherent topology, units, source/load assumptions and phase/RMS convention with checked limiting behavior.

criteria.title: Held-out evidence and competing models
criteria.adequate: Preserves selection choices and evaluates held-out observations, with specific evidence for each rejected or surviving model.

criteria.title: Energy and independent verification
criteria.adequate: Balances real power and provides a separately derived time-domain, analytic or numerical check with its error limits.

criteria.title: Reproducible bounded conclusion
criteria.adequate: Reports supported claims, non-uniqueness and model limits, with enough settings and evidence to reproduce the investigation.

rubric.proposedThreshold: At least 14 of 18, no zero, and at least two on provenance, model and energy. This is a self-study default, not an independent evaluation or NU grading standard.
rubric.declaration: The learner acknowledges that the observations are synthetic, that the rubric is self-assessed, and that report submission does not establish a physical laboratory result.

persistence: Versioned course-specific records use the existing shared progress repository and backup envelope. Explicit draft saves, conflicting edits, quota failures, unsupported record versions, immutable submitted records and user-requested revisions must remain recoverable. Do not overwrite PHS 231 notebooks or encode project completion as ordinary lesson evidence.
safety: The assigned procedure uses simulations only. Do not direct learners to household mains, exposed powered circuits, improvised high-voltage supplies, charged high-energy capacitors, hot coils or unknown laboratory equipment. Real equipment substitutions belong to a separately specified supervised experiment with its own ratings, isolation, discharge, thermal and measurement procedures.
independentVerification: Before release, derive each synthetic scenario with separate real sine/cosine equations; compare every exported row, uncertainty endpoint and power account; establish which candidate pairs are distinguishable on the chosen grid; include counterexamples to uniqueness. Exercise actual notebook submission, revision, reload and backup restoration in the browser.
